newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: BBAG acquires 50.2 pct of Romania Arbema.
newsitem.headline: BBAG acquires 50.2 pct of Romania Arbema.

text.p: Austria's biggest drinks group Oesterreichische Brau-Beteiligungs AG (BBAG) said on Thursday it would acquire 50.2 percent of Romanian brewer Arbema as part of its strategy to expand in eastern Europe.
"Our group's growth in the beer sector is happening exclusively abroad," BBAG chief executive Johannes Brandl told a news conference.
BBAG, struggling against stagnant beer consumption at home, will take control of Arbema in Arad, western Romania, through its Brau Union AG unit.
The group is already present as an exporter on the Romanian beer market through its flagship brands Kaiser and Goesser and owns breweries in Hungary and the Czech Republic.
BBAG will inject around 90 million schillings ($8.2 million) into Arbema in a capital increase to finance modernisation and boost output from 290,000 hectolitres annually.

"By the year 2000 Arbema should be producing some 600,000 hectolitres, putting it up there with Romania's biggest brewery," said BBAG export director Edmund Ranftl, who will take a place on Arbema's board.
Arbema, which employs 390 staff, will post sales of 115-120 million schillings this year.
Brandl forecast that BBAG's pre-tax profit this year would rise to around one billion schillings from 770 million in 1995, due mainly to the sale in the summer of its Coca-Cola business.

The 1.4 percent slide in domestic beer sales in the first 10 months of the year had been offset by a 10.3 percent increase abroad. Overall beverage sales rose less than one percent to 8.18 billion schillings, with beer accounting for 7.14 billion.
Arbema will brew BBAG's Kaiser and Goesser beers under licence, starting with Kaiser in the second half of 1997.

BBAG shares fizzed 2.7 percent higher on the news while Brau Union frothed up 3.8 percent. Both shares later drifted back and in late trade BBAG was eight schillings up at 748 while Brau Union stood 1.5 schillings down at 658.50.
-- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 25 ($ = 10.98 Austrian Schillings)
